points.description: Finds a valid base pair (P0,Q0) with P0 non-constant (e.g. P0(x)=x+1, Q0(x)=-x²/2+x/2+f, any f) AND checks it satisfies P0(Q0(x)-x-1)=Q0(P0(x)). Any other correct base pair is accepted, provided it is verified and has deg Q0 ≥ 2 (or can be used in the construction).

levels.says: Gives a correct base pair but does not verify it (or verification has a minor slip).

points.description: Gives a construction that raises the degree of P while keeping the equation valid. For example, with R=Q-x-1 and S any polynomial commuting with R (S∘R=R∘S, e.g. S=R iterated n times), set P1=P0∘S and keep Q. Other valid degree-raising constructions are acceptable.

levels.says: States a degree-raising idea but it is not fully specified or not shown to be usable (e.g. no commuting condition identified).

points.description: Proves that the constructed pair satisfies the equation. For the model construction: P1(R(x))=P0(S(R(x)))=P0(R(S(x)))=Q(P0(S(x)))=Q(P1(x)).

levels.says: Verification is mostly right but has a gap or unjustified step (e.g. commutation asserted without reason).

points.description: Shows the degree conditions: chooses the parameters so that deg P ≥ 2024 (e.g. R has degree 2, so R iterated 11 times has degree 2048, hence deg P1=2048) and deg Q ≥ 2, and states the conclusion.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a verified base pair, a degree-raising construction, a proof that the construction satisfies the identity, and the degree check. Any valid different construction earns the same marks. A base pair alone earns at most 2 marks. A construction that is described but not fully verified earns only part of P2 and P3.
rubric.answer_key:
Base solution: P0(x)=x+1, Q(x)=-x²/2+x/2. Check: P0(Q-x-1)=Q-x. Q(x+1)=-(x+1)²/2+(x+1)/2=-x²/2-x/2=Q(x)-x. ✓.
Let R(x)=Q(x)-x-1 (degree 2). Then P0∘R=Q∘P0.
Let S=R∘R∘…∘R (11 times). S commutes with R, and deg S=2^11=2048. Set P(x)=P0(S(x))=S(x)+1, deg 2048 ≥ 2024, and keep Q (deg 2).
Verify: P(Q(x)-x-1)=P0(S(R(x)))=P0(R(S(x)))=Q(P0(S(x)))=Q(P(x)) for all real x. ✓
So P(x)=R^{∘11}(x)+1 and Q(x)=-x²/2+x/2 satisfy the condition.
